summary: Jeffrey Davis Schoening specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 1991), studying under doctoral supervisor Collett Cox and advisor Sanghasen Singh.

Jeffrey Hopkins was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Wangyal, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and the 14th Dalai Lama, earning a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968-1972). He served at the University of Virginia (1973-2005).

Jeffrey J. Kripal specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Conception Seminary College and the University of Chicago (~1989-1993, PhD). In ~2002, he held a chair and department headship at Rice University, which he founded in 2014.

Jeffrey Kotyk specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University (MA 2015-2016) and Leiden University (PhD -2017) under James A. Benn. He held posts at McMaster University (attested 2019) and the University of Bologna.

Jeffrey Mehlman is a scholar of philosophy. He held positions at Cornell University (~1971-1974), Yale University, Johns Hopkins University (~1974-1980), and Boston University (~1984), alongside visiting professorships at Harvard, UC Berkeley, CUNY Graduate Center, Washington University, and MIT.

Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his BA and PhD (~1964-1970) at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held posts at the University of Toronto, Sigmund Freud Archives, UC Berkeley, and University of Auckland.

Jeffrey Newmark works in Japanology and history and archaeology. He studied at Harvard University (-1996) and the University of British Columbia (~2003-2009), and held a post at the University of Winnipeg (~2010).

Jeffrey S. Lidke is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held posts at Berry College and the University of Virginia, where he served as visiting assistant professor of religion (attested 2003).

Jeffrey Samuels is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia (attested 2002) under Karen Christina Lang. He served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Western Kentucky University (attested 2013).

Jeffrey Stout is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Brown University (~1968-1972) and Princeton University (~1972-1976, PhD), and served as a professor at Princeton University from 1976 to 2018.

Jeffrey Wayne Bass specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at UNC Wilmington, the University of Tennessee, and UCLA (PhD attested 2013) under Gregory Schopen. He held teaching posts at UCLA and UC San Diego (both attested 2013).

Jenkuan Shih specializes in Buddhist studies. Shih earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, having studied under MA supervisor Geshe Lhundup Sopa and doctoral supervisors Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi.

Jennifer Jung-Kim works in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, serving as assistant director (attested 2016) and lecturer (attested 2026).

Jens Braarvig is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held professorships at the Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology (~2000) and the University of Oslo (2003).

Jens Peter Laut is a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~2008-2020) and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~2008).

Jens Schlieter works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from the University of Bonn (~1993-1999) under Josef Simon. He held posts at Urania Berlin, Bonn, Munich, Bayreuth, and the University of Bern (~2009).

Jens-Uwe Hartmann is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Munich and Göttingen. He held professorships at the Free University of Berlin, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Munich (1999-2018).
Jeong-Eun Kim is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London (-2011) under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak.

Jerome Silbergeld is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He earned degrees from Stanford and the University of Oregon. He held professorships and administrative posts at the University of Washington (~1975-2001) and Princeton University (~2001-2016).

Jerzy Bańczerowski was a linguist who studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (~1956-1961). He spent his career there as department head (1969) and professor (1977-1991), and was a member of the Polish Academy of Sciences (~1989).
